items.summary: This change will improve the wearer's trust in subtitles, especially during critical interactions where accuracy is crucial. It will reduce cognitive load and social awkwardness, aligning with the core attractors of real-time subtitle clarity and low-friction assistance.

items.title: Confidence Display
items.summary: The refined confidence display will allow the wearer to better understand the reliability of each piece of assistance provided by the system. This increased clarity can lead to more effective use of the assistant, as the wearer is less likely to misinterpret uncertain information and can make quicker decisions based on the more detailed feedback.
items.probe: Choose one confidence display format for V1: label only or label plus short reason.

choices.label: Label Only
choices.description: Keep certainty display minimal and fast to parse.

choices.label: Label + Reason
choices.description: Expose a short reason to improve trust.

items.title: Memory/Cache Policy
items.summary: This change will enhance the accuracy of new-person recall by maintaining a fresh set of recently encountered entities in local memory, reducing the likelihood of outdated or irrelevant information being retrieved for new interactions. It also aligns with the core tension of balancing privacy and usefulness by ensuring that only relevant recent data is prioritized.
items.probe: Define a recency-first eviction policy for person memory objects based on their last interaction time.

choices.label: Smaller Cache
choices.description: Bias toward tighter local memory and lower load.

choices.label: Recency First
choices.description: Bias toward recent names and conversations.

items.title: Phone/Cloud Boundary
items.summary: By optimizing for real-time subtitle processing and fast face/name memory lookups, we can ensure that critical assistive behaviors are always available without latency issues, which enhances user trust and satisfaction. This balanced approach also helps in reducing unnecessary data transfers, conserving battery life, and maintaining privacy.
items.probe: Choose one phone-local versus cloud fallback boundary for face/name recall lookup in V1.

choices.label: Phone First
choices.description: Keep critical work local unless clearly necessary.

choices.label: Balanced Fallback
choices.description: Allow cloud assist for slower or richer lookups.

items.title: Visual Hierarchy
items.summary: By maintaining a clear distinction and prioritization between subtitles and one-line prompts, the wearer can maintain focus during conversations. This improves their ability to follow the conversation while also having quick access to important contextual cues like names or brief reminders, leading to a more streamlined and effective assistive experience.
items.probe: Define one visual priority rule between subtitles and one-line support where subtitles always take precedence unless they are too numerous or lengthy, in which case one-line support can appear as needed without crowding the display.

choices.label: Subtitles Dominate
choices.description: Keep subtitles above all other overlays.

choices.label: Balanced Overlay
choices.description: Allow prompts to share attention more evenly.
